brief: October 27-28 FOMC minutes show the committee held rates steady but almost all participants judged further hikes appropriate, with a couple weighing a December increase larger than 0.25pp. Inflation discussion centered on the AI buildout: demand for buildout inputs is outpacing supply and raising consumer goods prices, and many participants, up from some in September, called this a material inflation risk. Most saw inflation pressures as broad-based, and the vast majority saw upside risk even though most expect inflation to eventually decline to 2%. The labor market was judged stable near maximum employment despite a soft payrolls print, with wage growth consistent with the 2% target. A majority saw financial conditions tightening since September, and most flagged rapidly rising AI-related debt with hedge fund leverage as a channel that could amplify market stress, though several still called conditions supportive of growth. Since the meeting, San Francisco Fed President Daly said the bias for rates is up but gave no timing guidance, while Governor Waller said a 0.25pp December hike paired with guidance for a 0.25pp January hike is similar to his earlier floated 0.50pp December move. UBS expects 0.25pp hikes at both the December and January meetings.
